item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
A piece of wood was 40 cm long.

It was cut into 3 pieces.

The lengths in cm are

2x − 5

x + 7

x + 6

A. What is the length of the longest piece?

Answer: ____ cm

B. Show your work. If you use a calculator, you still must describe all the steps you used to obtain your answer.

descriptors: 15, with 4x + 8 = 40 or equivalent algebraic reasoning shown
8, with correct working shown or indication of x = 8 with correct working
x + 7, with correct working shown or indication of x = 8
15, with numerical (i.e., non-algebraic) reasoning shown
15 or x + 7 with no/incorrect work shown
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.stem: Which of these could represent the expression 2x + 3x?

options.label: A

reference_items.figure_description:
Four options showing visual representations:
- Option A shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into two segments by an interior vertical tick mark. The segment on the left is labeled x above, and the segment on the right is labeled 5 above.
- Option B shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into three segments by two interior vertical tick marks. From left to right, the segments are labeled 2, 3, and x above.
- Option C shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled x. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two parts, labeled 2 on the left and 3 on the right.
- Option D shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled 5. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two equal parts, each labeled x above.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A club has 86 members, and there are 14 more girls than boys. How many boys and how many girls are members of the club?

Show your work.

descriptors: 36 boys and 50 girls [Numerical method: e.g., 86 ÷ 2 = 43; 43 − 7 = 36 boys; 43 + 7 = 50 girls]
36 boys and 50 girls [Algebraic method: e.g., b + (b + 14) = 86; 2b = 72; b = 36; g = 36 + 14 = 50]
Other fully satisfactory method including “guess and check” with justification that 36 + 50 = 86
Either 36 boys or 50 girls, with or without another (incorrect) number
36 and 50 are given [Makes correct computations but reverses labels or does not include any mention of which is boys or girls]
36 boys and 50 girls, no method shown
Gives an algebraic equation or system of equations that can lead to the correct solution
Other partially correct
29 boys and 57 girls [Computes 86 ÷ 2 = 43; 43 − 14 = 29 and 43 + 14 = 57]
One of the numbers is 72 [Computes 86 − 14]
29 boys and 43 girls [Computes 43 − 14 = 29]
Gives an algebraic equation or system of equations that cannot lead to a correct solution
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
